# Numbers Renko

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Numbers Renko annotates Renko boxes with volume and elapsed-time information to support Wyckoff-style effort-versus-result reading. It helps distinguish a box requiring unusually large activity or time from an ordinary box, and aggregates volume into Weis waves for comparison with earlier waves. The author explicitly limits exact operation to Renko charts. The display therefore depends on synthetic brick construction, not just ordinary time candles. It is a discretionary market-structure aid; a large effort/no-result mark is not by itself a specified reversal entry.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable narrowly for per-brick volume/time baseline comparisons, large-value filtering and relative color categories, given an external Renko sequence. Weis-wave segmentation, exact threshold equality and brick construction remain caveats.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Given a supplied Renko sequence with brick volume V and elapsed time T, compute the user-period EMA baseline for each (SMA is selectable). Compare V or T with its corresponding baseline. Show-only-large mode retains values strictly above their baseline. Colors use successively larger relative categories: at most half baseline, above half, above one, above 1.5 and above two times baseline; the source does not fully settle equality at the higher boundaries.
- Accumulate Weis Wave Volume and divide it by wave length to estimate effort per brick.
- Compare current waves with preceding same/opposite-direction waves and flag unusually high effort or volume.

## Outputs and intended use

- Numbers inside boxes, configurable candle colors, arrows and square marks expose relative volume/time and wave effort.

## Parameters and stated settings

- EMA is the default averaging type, with SMA available; period and volume display divisor are configurable.
- Relative-volume color categories include above 2x, 1.5x, 1x and 0.5x average.
- No Result Ratio compares effort with its five-period SMA; Large Volume Ratio controls wave highlighting.
- Per-brick comparison takes the caller-selected average period and EMA/SMA choice; no default period is supplied. Volume and elapsed time may independently drive number and candle colors.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Renko brick path, volume allocation and elapsed time depend on feed and brick settings.
- The divisor example inconsistently writes 0.056 and 0.05, so its exact display arithmetic should not be inferred from prose.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Brick construction, wave reversal rule, default periods/ratios and complete trade rules are absent.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: Renko brick sequence with volume and elapsed time.

Repository input-class support: unavailable or unresolved. Ordinary OHLCV does not establish the exact synthetic brick path or allocated per-brick time/volume.

# [SK] Fibonacci Auto Trend Scouter

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** drawing-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Fibonacci Auto Trend Scouter automatically draws trend references from two timeframes and Fibonacci levels from the shorter horizon. It aims to reduce manual chart annotation while keeping both near-term and broader directional context visible. Optional sights connect a trend’s midpoint to the current price, offering a visual sense of displacement. The levels and lines evolve as high/low values change, so they are dynamic references rather than fixed historically available support/resistance. The source suggests reading direction and potential levels but supplies no systematic entry or confirmation test.

- High/low selection windows and the Fibonacci-level construction are undisclosed.

## How it works

- Detect highs/lows on two selected timeframes and update their trend lines as price changes.
- Color each line by its own direction and optionally draw midpoint-to-current-price sights.
- Use the shorter timeframe’s highest/lowest values to compute Fibonacci support/resistance levels.

## Outputs and intended use

- Trend lines/extensions, optional source labels and short Fibonacci lines with level/price tooltips support discretionary chart analysis.

- Two timeframes, line colors/styles/widths/extensions and labels are configurable.
- Sights default off; Fibonacci lines default short and can extend left/right.

- Updating extrema can shift historical-looking references; no non-repainting guarantee is established.

# Monte Carlo CT [SS]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Monte Carlo CT combines simulated price-path summaries with a separate Naive Bayes directional assessment. Instead of showing many random paths, it draws median and percentile trajectories, then asks the user to look for agreement between the simulated central path and the classifier. The central tendency is a model summary rather than the market’s most probable realized trajectory; the source’s tendency to call a median an average and its percentile tails two-sigma extremes should remain explicit qualifications.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Partly disclosed computation.** Random-walk estimators and classifier training labels/distributions are underspecified.

- Random-walk estimators and classifier training labels/distributions are underspecified.

## How it works

- Generate a lognormal random walk using estimated historical drift and volatility, then summarize simulated paths by horizon percentiles.
- Train a Gaussian-density Naive Bayes model on relative volume and momentum to estimate a positive-move posterior.
- Combine classifier table readings with the projected median slope for discretionary convergence analysis.

## Outputs and intended use

- Inspect the median, inner/outer percentile paths, posterior, relative volume and LONG/SHORT table state. The author suggests lower bullish bands as dip zones and the upper extreme as profit/stop context.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Displayed bands are 25/75 and 5/95 percentiles; LONG requires posterior above 50%. Moderate confidence is described between 40–60%, high above 70% or below 30%.
- Relative volume uses a 50-period average. Simulation lookback, forecast horizon and classifier training length are adjustable without defaults; lookback should at least match the forecast.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Analytical: assumed drift/volatility and Gaussian conditional densities can fail under regime shifts. Simulated percentile coverage is not realized-market coverage.
- Median versus mean language and two-sigma labeling are statistically imprecise; confidence categories also leave intermediate values unclear.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Path count, random seeding, anchoring, drift/volatility estimators, labels for training and treatment of ambiguous confidence ranges are unspecified.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: ohlcv.

Repository input-class support: available. Historical chart OHLCV supports the described analysis class; stochastic simulation additionally needs a reproducible random-state policy, and code parity is unverified.

# Trend Following Moving Averages

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Trend Following Moving Averages colors a moving average according to whether its recent movement is large enough relative to the wider price range to count as a trend. It aims to answer a common chart-reading question: whether price is trending rather than merely oscillating. Instead of relying only on the average’s slope, the method compares the range occupied by the average with a longer price channel. Color intensity then conveys the estimated trend strength. The author’s claim of compatibility across timeframes is an intention of this normalization, not demonstrated invariance.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for the channel-width trend flag with chosen MA, trend window and percentage rate. Final color-intensity ratio and optional regression smoothing remain outside this narrow computation.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Construct a channel from the selected moving average’s highest and lowest values over a trend-check period.
- Let MAWidth be the maximum minus minimum of the selected MA over Period to Check Trend. Let PriceWidth be the highest high minus lowest low over 300 bars. The disclosed trend flag is MAWidth > (Trend Channel Rate % / 100) × PriceWidth. This flag is independently defined even though the subsequent intensity mapping is not.
- Optionally apply linear regression to reduce noise.

## Outputs and intended use

- The moving-average line becomes lighter/darker according to channel-relative strength.
- Use color as trend-regime context; no crossing entry or exit is specified.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Price channel spans 300 bars. MA choices are EMA, SMA, RMA, WMA and VWMA.
- Period to Check Trend and Trend Channel Rate % are adjustable; optional linear regression is said to add one or two bars of latency.
- The narrow trend flag takes a chosen MA type/length, Period to Check Trend and Trend Channel Rate %. No numeric defaults for these inputs are supplied; disable optional regression for this scope.

## Failure modes and caveats

- A long price-channel outlier can suppress the trend ratio after current conditions change.
- Noise reduction can delay detection, and the exact strength calculation is incompletely described.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- MA length/default, exact strength ratio, regression window, direction coloring and order rules are missing.

- Independent supplied event example: r_t=RSI(close,14). Output +1.0 when r crosses above 70, −1.0 when r crosses below 30, otherwise 0.0. - Oversold/overbought crossings can persist within trends and are not automatic reversals.
- An external plot must preserve the signed interface; arbitrary indicator values are not compatible.

# Fair Value Gap Profile + Rolling POC [BigBeluga]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

FVG Profile + Rolling POC profiles where candle-gap formations concentrate, rather than simply where volume traded. It separates bullish and bearish gap counts and associated volume to describe directional imbalance by price region. A rolling peak/average and optional moving average add temporal context. The financial purpose is identifying repeated gap-formation zones for discretionary reaction analysis. Calling them inefficiencies does not prove an arbitrage opportunity or that price must revisit them. Several important mapping and rolling calculations remain conceptual rather than fully defined.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for raw bullish/bearish three-bar FVG events and their gap boundaries, supporting optional live boxes. Mitigation, profile mapping/volume, Rolling POC and Auto-MA equations remain outside this scope.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Independent three-bar FVG events: bullish when Low_t>High_(t−2), with raw gap boundaries [High_(t−2),Low_t]; bearish when High_t<Low_(t−2), with boundaries [High_t,Low_(t−2)]. These inequalities/boundaries define newly formed gaps independently of profile binning, volume assignment or later mitigation.
- Divide lookback price range into bins and assign each gap to its nearest bin; accumulate directional counts/volume.
- Normalize strength against the largest count and calculate an unspecified rolling peak-imbalance series with optional smoothing.

## Outputs and intended use

- Bull/bear profile segments, strength labels, delta/heatmap, live gap boxes and rolling POC/MA support zone analysis.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Strongest bin normalizes to 100%; lookback, bins, moving-average type/length and Auto scaling are configurable but defaults absent.
- Narrow raw-gap mode uses current and two-bars-back high/low with strict inequalities; live gap-box display is optional. The source supplies no additional raw-gap threshold or numeric defaults.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Gap-count density is not traded-volume density or actual resting liquidity.
- Moving bins and unspecified event-volume assignment can change apparent dominance.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Gap representative price, assigned volume, mitigation policy, rolling POC equation and Auto-length rule are absent.

## Idea and objective

Laguerre RSI uses a Laguerre-filter-based version of RSI to reduce the noise the author associates with conventional RSI. The intended interpretation combines threshold recrossings with a different meaning for sustained extremes: crossing back from an extreme is offered as a trade cue, while remaining pinned at an extreme is described as evidence of trend strength. ## Idea and objective

Fit rolling polynomial regressions and display their current endpoints as a polynomial LSMA with surrounding bands. The accompanying redrawn curve teaches the relationship between regression fitting and endpoint moving-average plots.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Unsmoothed rolling polynomial fit/endpoint is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Optionally prefilter the source with Ehlers’ two-pole Super Smoother. Use a local integer time axis over the sample window, form power-sum normal equations and solve coefficients by LU decomposition with forward/back substitution.
- Evaluate the polynomial across the window; offset coordinates within the same fitted equation if requested. Standard deviation above/below the curve forms channels, and current endpoints become LSMA/band time series.
- Approximate each fitted curve using line segments and show its equation; bar colors reflect source disparity from LSMA. Drawing updates can be limited to closes without changing calculation updates.
- Choose degree d and window N>d,with caller chronological x=1..N and supplied y. Solve A*a=b where A[j,k]=sum(x^(j+k)),b[j]=sum(x^j*y),j,k=0..d,using LU/forward/back substitution for nonsingular cases. Evaluate yhat(x)=sum(a[k]*x^k);endpoint=yhat(N). Source repeated-a1 typo remains documented;orientation is explicit study convention. Optional smoothing/bands and Pine numerical parity excluded.

## Outputs and intended use

- LSMA and bands can inform the caller’s analysis; the author discourages trading from the repeatedly redrawn historical curve.
- Equation/debug labels help inspect coefficients and numerical problems; the prose’s non-repainting endpoint claim remains unverified without code.
- Usable scope: Unsmoothed rolling polynomial fit/endpoint. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Source, optional smoothing, sample length, polynomial degree, regression offset, segment step and display controls.
- Default sample is 100 and drawing step 10; each of three curves uses 10 segments.

## Failure modes and caveats

- High-degree normal equations can be ill-conditioned despite local coordinates; overfit and floating-point roundoff increase with degree/window.
- The written polynomial repeats coefficient a1 for the squared term, a typographical ambiguity inconsistent with its otherwise general coefficient construction.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Band standard-deviation definition/multiplier, Super Smoother settings, LU pivoting and exact time orientation are unspecified.

## Idea and objective

Buyers & Sellers Profile + Dynamic S/R refines confirmed swing levels using nearby volume-profile evidence. It aims to combine structural pivots with actual historical participation proxies instead of drawing every swing. Candle volume is distributed by price-range overlap and split by closing location, explicitly as an estimate rather than true footprint data. A nearby profile node can pull a pivot-derived level toward stronger participation, while a second score incorporates candle absorption/rejection. The result supports discretionary retest monitoring, not proof of institutional buying or guaranteed support.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

**Partly disclosed computation.** Proportional overlap and buyShare are disclosed, but no source rule defines the profile row-domain endpoints/boundaries. Adding caller-supplied row intervals would extend the source input contract; a complete rolling profile/POC is therefore still incomplete.

- The rolling profile price-domain endpoints and row-boundary construction are unspecified.
- Zero-range candle allocation is unspecified.

## How it works

- For a nonzero-range candle, buyShare=(Close−Low)/(High−Low), sellShare=1−buyShare. For a defined profile row interval [a,b], the stated proportional overlap allocation corresponds to Volume×max(0,min(High,b)−max(Low,a))/(High−Low), then multiply by the respective shares. Sum row volume over the lookback and choose the maximum-volume row as POC. The source does not define the actual row-domain endpoints, equal-spacing rule or zero-range allocation; this formula therefore describes allocation conditional on rows, not a fully specified published profile.
- Search around confirmed pivots in ATR distance and score node strength, local prominence, directional volume and proximity.
- Blend raw pivot toward chosen node, score profile/absorption/volume/wick evidence, merge nearby same-side levels and invalidate on buffered closes.

## Outputs and intended use

- Rolling split profile, POC and scored support/resistance lines show participation-confirmed structure.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Profile evidence weights 50/20/20/10%; final score weights 50/20/15/15%.
- Lookback/rows, swing length, search/min-node/evidence/pull/score, level cap, merge and break ATR are inputs; defaults absent.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Closing-location allocation is an estimate and zero-range candles require handling.
- Confirmed pivots and historical profile reconstruction must use information available at evaluation time.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Subscore normalization, pull-strength mapping, absorption equation, ATR defaults and merge policy are absent.
- The profile price-domain endpoints and row-boundary spacing are not stated; Rows only controls their number. Zero-range candles and maximum-row ties also lack conventions.

Separate risk-on/off alerts identify crossings into and back out of outer regions. The optional historical performance mode is described as a diagnostic simulation with sizing and direction controls, but no fill/cost details are provided. Consequently the channel concept is clearer than either the persistent trend-state engine or the reported performance calculations.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for caller-parameterized SMA/EMA-centered absolute-deviation EMA bands and explicitly named band-crossing events. Full FRAMA/state/backtest behavior remains incomplete.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Narrow ordinary-MA envelope: choose source X and SMA or EMA center M with length L. Let D=EMA(|X−M|,K), Upper=M+mD and Lower=M−mD for selected deviation length K and multiplier m. Risk-on long is a price cross above Upper; risk-off long a cross back below Upper; risk-on short a cross below Lower and risk-off short a cross back above Lower. These are crossing events, not an inferred persistent trend-state machine.
- Calculate selected MA and EMA of absolute deviation from it, then multiply deviation for upper/lower bands.
- Classify excursions above/below bands and track corresponding trend flips/risk-on/off crossings.

- Choose SMA/EMA, source, center length L, deviation EMA length K and multiplier m; numeric defaults are not supplied. FRAMA, intrabar repaint option, full trend-state persistence and backtest accounting are outside this scope.

- Intrabar mode can repaint.

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

## Idea and objective

Oscillator Workbench translates oscillator behavior into price-chart channels so traders can explore configurations in market context. It normalizes an oscillator’s position above or below its centerline, weights a price source with that percentage, and compares a weighted average with an unweighted reference. Separate divergence channels mark transition/consolidation regions without assigning an immediate bullish or bearish prediction. Direction follows later price breaches. The author suggests aligned strong states as one possible use, while emphasizing that settings must fit the reader’s methodology and that a neutral divergence region is generally a no-trade area.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for alternate close-RSI20 versus close-change divergence channels, including high/low expansion and whole-bar breaches. Default weighted-price channel, cap, strong-state labels and complex oscillator modes remain underspecified.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Track historical oscillator extrema separately above/below the centerline and convert relative position into signed weight; optionally include relative volume.
- Average original and weighted price sources with the same MA settings and cap weighted displacement.
- Detect mismatched slopes, form/expand a channel from divergence-bar prices until breached, and classify states by breach direction and oscillator-channel alignment.
- Independent alternate mode: use close-based RSI of length 20 and flag a divergence when the polarity of its one-bar change differs from close-to-close price-change polarity. At a divergence, save that bar high/low as channel top/bottom. Further divergences before breach expand top upward or bottom downward only when their extremes lie outside the current channel. After a breach, the next divergence starts a new channel.
- For default whole-bar breaches, bullish means the bar low is above channel top; bearish means the bar high is below channel bottom. An unbreached channel is neutral. Strong-state labels still require the separately underspecified weighted oscillator channel and are excluded from this usable alternate-channel scope.

## Outputs and intended use

- Oscillator channel, divergence levels, bar colors, optional closing-bar markers/alerts and Data Window raw values support exploratory analysis.
- Strong-to-ordinary trend-state weakening can motivate discretionary stop tightening, not an automatic reversal.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Thirty internal oscillators or an external plot with specified centerline are selectable.
- Defaults use close-based RSI 20 and ALMA 20, oscillator-only weight, three-standard-deviation cap, divergence-bar high/low and whole-bar breach conditions.
- Cap can instead use ATR; channel prices, divergence mode, bias estimation, coloring and marker filters are adjustable.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Early-history normalization is explicitly fragile. Volume-dependent choices fail when volume is unavailable.
- Realtime values change; the author says markers appear only at bar close, which does not independently verify all historical behavior.

Ties/zero ranges require caller conventions.
- Aggregate first open,maximum high,minimum low,last close by block. Estimate buy/sell via close-location fractions or intrabar data; compare block highs/lows for trend and average wicks/body changes for pressure. - Normalize tail, volatility, credit and positioning components with percentile ranks and absolute adjustments, then combine them with configurable weights.

## Idea and objective

Fractional EMA Kalman Filter D7 conditions price through deliberately reactive fractional-EMA stages, then uses a single-state Kalman-style correction to form smoother estimates. Baseline and faster versions are plotted together to make the response tradeoff visible; “fractional” here describes sub-integer EMA lengths, not necessarily fractional calculus.

# Volume and Price Z-Score [Multi-Asset] - By Leviathan

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Volume and Price Z-Score screens assets by how unusual current price and activity are relative to their own histories and, optionally, relative to the group. It distinguishes a single-bar anomaly from persistent averaged deviations and cross-sectional outliers. Multiple displays let the reader compare price-volume alignment, divergence and unusual participation without imposing one trade interpretation. The source correctly notes that financial price and volume are generally not normally distributed, so standardized distances should not be converted into normal-theory probabilities. OBV mode changes the question from activity magnitude to a cumulative directional-volume proxy.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for ordinary Current/Average price and regular-volume z-scores and price-minus-volume delta with a chosen averaging length and default 20-bar normalization window. Relative-group normalization and exact variance convention remain caveats.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- For ordinary Current mode, calculate each selected price or regular-volume observation minus its rolling mean, divided by the corresponding rolling standard deviation, over the chosen lookback (default 20 bars). Average mode takes the custom-length average of that z-score series. Delta equals price z-score minus volume z-score. Dispersion sample convention and zero-dispersion handling remain caveats.
- Relative mode standardizes a symbol’s z-score against group z-score behavior, although its exact denominator is not given.
- Choose regular volume or OBV and optionally subtract volume z-score from price z-score.

## Outputs and intended use

- Scatterplot maps price z-score horizontally and volume vertically; squares guide standardized distance.
- Paired columns/circles, delta columns and history heatmaps expose cross-asset anomalies and alignment.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Advertised coverage is 200 symbols; current z-score mean lookback defaults to 20 bars.
- Current, Average and Relative modes, custom averaging length, volume/OBV, display type and heatmap gradient are selectable.
- Scatter guides use ±1/2/3 SD; column/circle display range is described as -4 to 4.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Cross-sectional outliers depend on universe selection and aligned timestamps.
- OBV is a candle-direction proxy; price-volume convergence is not causal proof or a guaranteed signal.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Symbol universe, dispersion conventions, relative-mode formula, zero-variance handling, OBV initialization and order rules are missing.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: multi-asset OHLCV histories, selected symbol universe.

# Stop Loss Cascades (Breakouts) [Kioseff Trading]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Estimate where hidden stop pressure might concentrate and contextualize possible breakout cascades. The indicator explicitly models unobservable stops rather than measuring actual stop locations, quantities or live order-book depth.

- Swing eligibility/lifetime, ATR period/scaling, volume distribution weights, trigger/retirement conditions and historical move horizon are undisclosed.

## How it works

- The swing model assigns all classified buy volume to the closest active low and sell volume to the closest active high after formation, producing comparative potential-stop magnitudes. Direction derives from higher/lower close classification.
- The volatility-at-entry model distributes directional volume over multiple timeframe ATR distances. Triggered clusters receive size-classification graphics; nearby modeled buy/sell clusters populate a table.
- For typical-move context, log-transform current and historical cluster magnitudes and choose neighbors within a spacing-based tolerance or the closest match, then retrieve their associated historical moves. A ratio meter sums active and triggered buy/sell clusters.

## Outputs and intended use

- Cluster zones, trigger graphs, nearest-level data and directional ratios support situational awareness around breakout areas.
- Historical similar-size outcomes are explicitly descriptive, sometimes having very few neighbors; they are not forecasts or proof of latent positions.

- Model choice and lower-timeframe granularity defaulting to one minute; finer seconds/ticks trade coverage for detail.
- Volatility distribution references1m,5m,15m,30m,1h,4h and ATR multiples1,1.5,2.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Assigning all volume to stops ignores exits, hedges, alternative stops and positions already closed. Exaggerated magnitudes are relative proxies.
- Resting liquidity can absorb triggered flow; modeled cluster size cannot guarantee breakout acceleration.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

## How it works

- For supplied ordered live platform updates, reset the update index at each new candle and number successive observations 1, 2, and so on. Place a dot at that index in tick-up/down mode; progression mode places the observations on the candle using successively spaced text.
- Compare each observed price with the preceding tick price: higher is green, lower red and unchanged dimmed blue. A separate start symbol identifies the first update of each candle. Platform updates can reflect either price or volume changes and are not guaranteed to be individual trades.

## Outputs and intended use

- Green/red/blue means higher/lower/unchanged tick price. Separate start symbols and optional hidden candles help identify where each bar's update sequence begins. This is live microstructure visualization, not a historical reconstruction.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Maximum displayed dots are five hundred. Dot/custom symbol and candle display are configurable. The author considers intervals above five minutes generally impractical, particularly for active symbols.

## Failure modes and caveats

- The author reports possible undrawn ticks, imperfect label price placement and overlap into following candles. Label limits delete earlier history; platform updates are not necessarily individual exchange executions.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Persistence/deduplication, exact positioning and retention rules need code. A live update feed is essential and cannot be recovered from ordinary bars.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Each active constituent receives equal weight; market-cap weighting is explicitly reserved for a future enhancement. Momentum is percentage price change over a lookback.
- Modes display the group composite, benchmark momentum, or their difference. Alternative RSI, stochastic, Williams %R and CCI transformations provide different oscillator views.
- Breadth counts constituents with positive momentum. Threshold and zero-line alerts summarize direction and relative leadership.
- For each active constituent ROC_i=100*(P_i[t]-P_i[t-n])/P_i[t-n],requiring nonzero lagged price. Composite=sum(ROC_i)/active_count;breadth%=100*count(ROC_i>0)/active_count. Benchmark differential=composite-benchmark_ROC. Caller defines n and complete active set;this fixed named basket does not imply historical membership reconstruction. Alternative transforms/smoothing excluded.

## Outputs and intended use

- Oscillator, component/status/breadth table and hidden component plots support analysis and downstream testing.
- The author proposes exposure timing and breadth deterioration monitoring but supplies no allocation or execution rule.
- Usable scope: Raw ROC/equal-weight momentum and breadth. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Default momentum lookback is 14; bullish/bearish thresholds default to +2%/-2%, relative thresholds +1%/-1%.
- Momentum period range 5–100, smoothing 1–50; breadth above 60% is strong and below 40% weak.

## Failure modes and caveats

- A fixed current-name basket can introduce selection bias in historical research; the prose does not define a historical membership policy.
- Alternative oscillators have incompatible natural units, making percentage threshold interpretation ambiguous.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Transformation scaling, smoothing method and order, missing-constituent policy and exact benchmark/security contracts are unspecified.

## Data requirements

## How it works

- Volume quartiles and a high-percentile threshold categorize bars, display dispersions and measure subsequent returns. Successive high-volume observations can receive a regression channel, and a time anchor can start VWAP.

- Volume-aggregation bars form when cumulative chart-timeframe volume reaches a threshold, carrying excess forward. Gap tracking records partial fills, completion delays and directional statistics, sorting unfilled gaps by price distance.
- Accumulate supplied chart-bar volume against caller positive threshold Q. Mark a threshold event when cumulative volume reaches/exceeds Q;carry the remainder forward. Event timing occurs at observed chart bars,not synthetic tick fills. Multiple events/overshoot price mapping,automatic thresholds,range/gap/quartile outputs remain unqualified.

- OHLC approximations cannot recreate tick-level range or volume bars. Small thresholds can produce misleading synthetic structure.
- Conditional returns following high volume are descriptive and sensitive to sample overlap and regime; they do not prove a tradable edge.

# Intraday Volume Swings

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Intraday Volume Swings records price extremes reached during stretches of rising volume, then carries the day’s final selected high and low into the following session. It aims to distinguish participation-supported swings from arbitrary daily extremes, providing possible retracement or support/resistance references. Current-day candidates can also be displayed but may later be replaced by more extreme qualifying swings.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Volume/price runs and next-day extrema is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Define qualifying runs with increasing volume and higher highs or lower lows over at least three bars.
- Keep the highest high-swing and lowest low-swing during the day and plot those final references on the next day.
- Detect at least3 bars with strictly increasing volume and strictly higher highs or lower lows. Within caller day keep highest qualifying high-swing/lowest qualifying low-swing; carry completed values to following day. Ties terminate strict runs under explicit study convention; live candidates may change.

## Outputs and intended use

- Inspect prior-day swing references and optional developing intraday levels for areas of interest, without a specified entry trigger.
- Usable scope: Volume/price runs and next-day extrema. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Minimum run length is three bars; current-day display is optional. Other defaults and session settings are not disclosed.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Analytical: developing levels are provisional and price can cross a prior participation level without reversing.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Exact consecutive comparison rules, day/session boundary, equal-value handling and swing finalization are unspecified.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: ohlcv.
